rules.sentence: To diagnose hypoglycemia, symptoms and blood sugar levels must improve with the administration of exogenous glucose.
In patients without diabetes mellitus, this is usually manifested at glucose levels below 50 mg/dl.

In patients with diabetes or chronically elevated blood glucose levels, symptoms may manifest at other levels; specifically, people with chronically elevated blood glucose levels may experience hypoglycemic symptoms at blood glucose levels typically defined as normal.
It is, therefore, paramount that patients with any paroxysmal spell or loss of consciousness receive a fingerstick glucose test.
Diagnosis is by clinical history and CT imaging, although MRI may be more specific for secondary trauma.
Management is to reduce intracranial pressure and edema.
